BRD-01.evidence: Mounted PostgreSQL create-board tests pass; default columns are inserted in the same transaction. No failure-injection rollback test.

BRD-02.evidence: Mounted role/list/name/version tests pass; writes use grant lock and optimistic version. No archive behavior claimed here.

BRD-03.evidence: Mounted snapshot/filter/count test passes. Snapshot cursor is only position/id and is not revision/filter-bound.

BRD-05.evidence: Mounted exact-set reorder and placement tests pass. No parallel reorder or stale-page test.

BRD-06.evidence: Mounted active/restorable/final-column guards pass. Expired trashed references remain a nonblocking lifecycle edge.

BRD-07.evidence: Malformed cursor is rejected, but valid old cursor has no board revision/filter binding; stale order/filter changes cannot return STALE_CURSOR and can omit/duplicate cards.

tests.result: Supplied builder log reports typecheck, build including Worker dry-run, API tests and contracts tests succeeded; not independently rerun as a full check.

security.reason: Shared receipt path rechecks and locks current project grant before replay; source is sound, but required board-route revoked/demoted replay regression is absent, so security minimum 9 is not met.

correctness.reason: Core flows pass; stale board cursors are accepted across order/filter changes, contradicting BRD-07 and API.md. Expired-trash column deletion has an unresolved generic FK failure edge.

integrity.reason: Transactions, optimistic versions and grant/idempotency locks are present, but continuation pages are not a stable snapshot and concurrent board mutation behavior is not exercised.

tests.reason: Reviewer typecheck and all 16 focused PostgreSQL tests pass. Required stale-after-change, board revoke/demote replay, same-key concurrency and receipt retention assertions are missing.

maintainability.reason: Typed contracts, parameterized SQL and clear route/adapter separation; cursor encoding omits context needed by its contract and endpoint replay regressions are incomplete.

operations.reason: Limits are present, but stale traversal can silently omit work, placement/snapshot performance is unmeasured, and expired references can surface as database failures.

findings.description: BRD-07 cursor contains only position and id; current board/order/filter revision is not bound. The query applies an old tuple to the changed result set, accepting stale cursors and potentially omitting or duplicating cards. Test rejects malformed cursor only.
findings.impact: A teammate changing order or filters while the user pages can cause cards to disappear from traversal or repeat without refresh notification.
findings.counterevidence: Normal continuation and malformed-cursor tests pass; those do not exercise a valid cursor after a board/filter change.
findings.fix: Bind cursor to board/order revision and normalized filters; return STALE_CURSOR when context changes; add mounted PostgreSQL order/filter-change tests.

findings.description: Repair criteria require mounted PostgreSQL tests for replay after grant removal/demotion, same-key concurrency and receipt-body inspection. The BRD suite has only ordinary sequential board create replay/collision. Shared card tests do not prove each board route's required replay family coverage.
findings.impact: The implementation change fixing a previous revoked-replay disclosure lacks regression evidence on the affected board routes and persistent receipt contents.
findings.counterevidence: All mounted board routes call the shared grant-locking receipt helper; broader card tests exercise role recheck and same-key writes.
findings.fix: Add BRD route tests for access removal/demotion, parallel same-key request, conflicting key and persisted receipt inspection.

findings.description: Adapter blocks only restorable trashed cards then deletes a referenced column. Expired but unpurged rows still reference the column under ON DELETE RESTRICT, resulting in a database constraint failure rather than a deliberate domain response. Existing test only covers a restorable trash row.
findings.impact: Column deletion can fail as an internal server error while expired trash waits for purge.
findings.counterevidence: BRD-06 explicitly names active/restorable cards; the expiring row is no longer restorable, so this is outside its narrow blocker wording.
findings.fix: Clarify the expired-trash policy and return a stable conflict or safely detach/purge according to that policy, with a PostgreSQL regression.

hardBlockers: F-01: BRD-07 valid stale cursors are not detected after order/filter changes.
F-02: Frozen repair criteria's required mounted board replay regression evidence is incomplete.
coverageGaps: No valid cursor-after-reorder or cursor-after-filter-change regression.
